atlas.title: 曼彻斯特
atlas.caption: Coupland Street 物理实验室 · α 散射

labEmbed.title: α 粒子散射 · 实验台

text.en: Manchester, Coupland Street, nineteen-nine. In the dark room Geiger and Marsden are counting flashes on a zinc-sulphide screen. Most of the α-particles from the source go nearly straight through the thin foil — the scene looks quieter than it is.
text.zh-Hans: 一九〇九年，曼彻斯特 Coupland Street。暗室里，盖革和马斯登对着硫化锌屏一闪一闪地数。从放射源出来的 α 粒子，绝大多数几乎笔直穿过薄箔——场面安静得过分。

claim.citation: H. Geiger & E. Marsden, Proc. R. Soc. A 82 (1909) 495–500
claim.notes: cite fact-gm1909-paper / fact-gm1909-zns-method / fact-gm1909-forward-majority. Name Geiger & Marsden's labour; they do not speak.

text.en: But a few are turned through large angles — some even come back toward the source. They call that diffuse reflection. The scintillations on the screen are counted one by one by Geiger and Marsden; my part is to give an account of what those counts mean. Early on, people slighted the α-rays because they barely penetrate — the more we measure, the less we can treat them as a trifle.
text.zh-Hans: 可是有少数偏转很大——有的甚至折回源一侧。他们称之为漫反射。屏上的闪光由盖革和马斯登一颗一颗来数；我负责说明这些计数意味着什么。早年有人轻视 α 射线，就因为它几乎穿不透——量得越多，就越不能把它当小事。

claim.citation: H. Geiger & E. Marsden, Proc. R. Soc. A 82 (1909) 495–500
claim.notes: cite fact-gm1909-diffuse-reflection. Credit counting; no ledger slang.

text.en: The arrangement is spare: a thin metal foil, a zinc-sulphide screen, a microscope. Geiger and Marsden sit in the dark and count flashes one by one — dull work, not a lecture. Most of the α-particles go nearly forward. How is a diffuse sphere of positive electricity supposed to throw a few of them so far aside?
text.zh-Hans: 装置很简单：一张薄金属箔，一块硫化锌屏，一台显微镜。盖革和马斯登坐在暗处一颗一颗数闪光——枯燥，不是讲课。绝大多数 α 几乎朝前飞。弥散的正电球，怎么能把少数几条路径甩得那么远？

claim.citation: Geiger & Marsden 1909, pp. 496–497 (ZnS method, thin foil); era-op-thomson-uniform-sphere
claim.notes: cite fact-gm1909-zns-method / fact-gm1909-geometry / era-op-thomson-uniform-sphere. No invented fractions. Geiger & Marsden named, do not speak.

text.en: Take it as a working hypothesis for now: the positive electricity nearly gathered in a very small region at the centre of the atom — a concentrated central charge. Most paths barely deflect; a few deflect violently. That looks more like striking a strong local field than piling up weak turns inside a diffuse sphere of positive electricity. The evidence is still lengthening; until we have a more decisive proof, I will not speak as if the case were closed.
text.zh-Hans: 先当作工作假说：正电几乎聚在原子中心很小一块——集中的中心电荷。绝大多数路径几乎不偏，少数却偏得很狠。这更像撞上很强的局域场，而不像在弥散正电球里一点点叠出来。证据还在加长；在更干脆的证明到来以前，我不会说得好像案子已经结了。

claim.notes: cite fact-ruth1911-central-charge. Period term central charge; no nucleus banner. Working-hypothesis register for 1909 scene.

text.en: Textbooks later call this the nuclear model of the atom: nearly all the mass and positive charge packed into a tiny centre, with electrons outside. In the laboratory of this period one more often said central charge. Either way, a plum-pudding picture with positive electricity smeared through the whole atomic volume cannot account for these rare but stubborn large-angle deflections.
text.zh-Hans: 后来教材把这叫做原子的核式结构：质量和正电荷几乎都挤在很小的中心，电子在外围。这个时期的实验室里，更常说「中心电荷」。无论如何，正电涂满整个原子体积的枣糕图景，解释不了这些稀少却顽固的大角偏转。

claim.citation: 人教版选必三 第四§3–§4（教材用语：核式结构）
claim.notes: Textbook register; nuclear model wording OK here only. Align era-op-nucleus-word-anachronism.

text.en: Later storytellers love the picture of a fifteen-inch shell striking tissue paper and bouncing back. It sounds fine — but that is late recollection, not a line from the nineteen-nine dark-room notebooks. We should not live on legends. Shall we try it ourselves at the apparatus?
text.zh-Hans: 后人爱讲那个画面：十五英寸炮弹打在薄纸上又弹回来。听着痛快——可那是事后回忆，不是一九〇九年暗室本子上的原话。别靠传说过日子。要不要自己上实验台试一次？

text.en: The bench is there. Change the foil if you like; watch whether the large-angle flashes stay scarce and stubborn. I will not close the case from a speech. Try the apparatus, then we can talk of a central charge again.
text.zh-Hans: 台子在那儿。箔厚你尽管改；看大角闪光是不是依旧又少又顽固。我不会靠一篇讲话把案子结掉。先试装置，再说中心电荷。

claim.citation: Invite to labEmbed; aligned to fact-gm1909-diffuse-reflection + era-op-caution-before-central-charge
claim.notes: Cold-open close: send player to apparatus. interpretation.

text.en: So those are the counts from the bench. Most paths still run nearly forward; a few large-angle flashes still turn up. Same contrast the dark-room notebooks keep repeating — quiet majority, stubborn minority. Does that match what you just saw?
text.zh-Hans: 台子上的计数就是这样。绝大多数路径仍几乎朝前；少数大角闪光仍会出现。暗室本子里反复出现的对照——安静的大多数，顽固的少数。跟你刚看见的对得上吗？

claim.notes: VN-lab-03 return. afterLab. No invented fractions.

text.en: Scarce is not none. Geiger and Marsden counted this class of event on the screen; the notebook is not ornament. If your run showed even a handful of large deflections through a thin foil, you are looking at the same trouble a diffuse positive sphere does not like to admit.
text.zh-Hans: 少，不等于没有。盖革和马斯登在屏上数过这类事件；本子不是摆设。若你这一轮在薄箔上哪怕只见到几回大偏转，你面对的就是弥散正电球不愿承认的麻烦。

claim.citation: H. Geiger & E. Marsden, Proc. R. Soc. A 82 (1909) 495–500
claim.notes: cite fact-gm1909-diffuse-reflection. Credit counting; Geiger does not speak.

text.en: I still take a concentrated central charge as the working hypothesis — positive electricity gathered in a very small region — not a slogan and not a closed case. What we press next is how the pattern changes with foil thickness, and whether large angles stay too common for compound scattering alone. Until a more decisive proof, keep what was seen apart from what is guessed.
text.zh-Hans: 我仍把集中的中心电荷当作工作假说——正电聚在很小一块——不是口号，也不是结案。接下来要压的是：箔厚一变，图样怎么变；大角是否仍多到单靠多次散射说不过去。在更干脆的证明到来以前，看见的和猜的，先分开放。

claim.notes: cite fact-ruth1911-central-charge + era-op-compound-scattering-default + era-op-caution-before-central-charge. Period term central charge.

text.en: The laboratory has given you a readout, not a verdict. Forward majority and rare large angles are what was seen; central charge is still a working account. Textbooks later say nuclear model; that word is not the banner of this room. The lodge is for sorting those two piles before you come back to the foil.
text.zh-Hans: 实验室给的是读数，不是判决。前进占多数、大角稀少，是看见的；中心电荷仍是工作说明。后来教材说核式结构；那个词不是这间屋子的旗号。租屋里先把这两堆分开，再回箔前。

claim.citation: 人教版选必三 第四§3–§4；era-op-nucleus-word-anachronism
claim.notes: Narrator may use nuclear model. afterLab close.

text.en: At night I read the day's scintillation counts again. Most paths nearly forward, a few at large angles — the diffuse positive sphere of the plum-pudding picture never seems to pile up so violent a deflection. The central-charge sketch, though, can make sense of those sharp flashes on the screen. The dull numbers from daylight start to bite after dark.
text.zh-Hans: 夜里我又把白天的闪烁计数读了一遍。绝大多数几乎朝前，少数大角——枣糕图景里那团弥散正电，怎么也堆不出这么猛的偏转。中心电荷那张草图，倒能说明屏上那些刺眼的闪光。白天乏味的数字，夜里才开始咬人。

text.en: If we keep the plum-pudding picture — positive electricity smeared through the whole volume, large angles only as the tail of many weak turns — what would the apparatus have to hide? The rare returning paths are still in the notebook. I can restate the counts. I cannot make the diffuse sphere produce them.
text.zh-Hans: 若仍守着枣糕图景——正电涂满整个体积，大角只是多次弱偏转的尾巴——装置还得藏住什么？本子里那些稀少的折回路径还在。我可以重述计数，却没法让弥散球把它们变出来。

claim.notes: Watson aide: press the era foil without inventing numbers.

text.en: Large angles are scarce — everyone grants that — yet they are not zero. Geiger and Marsden put those rare flashes into the notebook; they are not there for ornament. If the positive charge is truly concentrated at the centre, those rare large-angle paths can stand; if we cling to a diffuse sphere plus compound scattering alone, the returning paths become a nuisance. I want an account that will bear the apparatus and the foil thickness — not a neat slogan.
text.zh-Hans: 大角很少——谁都承认——可绝不是零。盖革和马斯登把那些稀少闪光记进本子；那不是装饰。若正电真的集中在中心，那些稀少大角路径才站得住；若仍死守弥散球加多次散射，折回的路径就成了麻烦。我要的是经得起装置和箔厚的说明，不是一句漂亮口号。

claim.citation: Lodge night review — aligned to fact-gm1909-diffuse-reflection + fact-ruth1911-central-charge

text.en: Tomorrow we go back to foil thickness and the angular pattern. Central charge remains a working hypothesis; I will not treat it as dogma until the apparatus has had another say. Sleep on the distinction: what Geiger and Marsden counted, and what I am still only proposing.
text.zh-Hans: 明天回箔厚和角分布。中心电荷仍是工作假说；装置没再发言以前，我不会把它当教条。先分清：盖革和马斯登数到的，和我此刻只是在提出的。

claim.notes: Caution before dogma. Geiger named, does not speak.

text.en: In the lodge we first keep what was seen apart from what is guessed: observation here, hypothesis there. Tomorrow, back in the laboratory — change the foil thickness, watch whether the angular pattern shifts. Asking the apparatus again beats arguing under the lamp.
text.zh-Hans: 租屋里先把看见的和猜的分开：观测归观测，假说归假说。明天回实验室——改箔厚，看角分布变不变。再问装置，胜过在灯下空争。
